source.title: Kernel and Rich Regimes in Overparametrized Models
source.authors: Blake E. Woodworth; Suriya Gunasekar; J. Lee; E. Moroshko; P. Savarese; Itay Golan; Daniel Soudry; N. Srebro

page_placements.theme: Initialization and training history affect fitted solutions

record.tranche_reason: The study reports test-error results from training neural networks on natural datasets while varying initialization scale, a condition not named by the supplied versions.
record.gate_note: The MNIST and CIFAR-10 results vary initialization scale, not random-label capacity, width past interpolation, architecture comparisons, optimizer choice, batch size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example removal. Cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures how initialization scale affects generalization and analyzes width in matrix factorization. Neither tests any supplied version: there is no random-label comparison, neural-network width sweep, matched architecture comparison, optimizer comparison, batch-size comparison, dropout intervention, magnitude-aware sharpness measurement, or memorized-example removal. Section 7 cites V2's original source but does not reproduce its width comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors analytically characterize initialization-dependent implicit bias in diagonal linear models, analyze the joint role of width and initialization in matrix factorization, and demonstrate analogous transitions in nonlinear networks. Their neural-network experiments suggest good performance just outside the kernel regime, while smaller initialization can create optimization difficulties; this is not a universal claim that smaller initialization always improves generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies initialization scale and studies implicit bias and generalization; it does not apply the methods or measures of the supplied claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization scale; depth in synthetic experiments; dataset and architecture across the MNIST and CIFAR-10 experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed width, MNIST networks attain 100% training accuracy but approximately 1.4% test error at small initialization and 2.4% at large initialization; CIFAR-10 experiments show a similar initialization dependence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization scale affects generalization even among networks that perfectly fit their training data.

fits_no_version.finding: Training only the MNIST output layer yields 2.7% test error, compared with approximately 1.4% when training the full network at small initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature learning outside the kernel regime can improve generalization over fixed random features.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic ReLU regression experiments show that leaving the kernel regime can lower test error, with initialization scale and depth controlling the transition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization scale and depth affect feature learning and generalization in synthetic regression.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 6 shows that matrix-factorization width and initialization jointly determine the kernel-to-rich transition; low-rank matrix recovery requires sufficiently small initialization relative to width.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The generalization consequences of widening matrix factorizations depend on how initialization scales with width.

record.problems: Several neural-network results are presented only in figures without numerical values in the text. MNIST learning rates were selected separately by validation error for each initialization scale; CIFAR-10 uses one stated learning rate and no data augmentation. The synthetic task uses a small training set and is not a natural-data classification task.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows omitted. Figure-only test-error values are retained as figure-only rows because the text does not provide the plotted numbers.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting capacity and natural-label generalization, including chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test error as ReLU-network width increases beyond the width required for zero training error. Matrix-factorization width results do not establish this behavior.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD generalization and dependence on tuning or optimizer modifications.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and their dependence on training-set size, dropout strength, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures. Tangent-feature cosine distance is a different measure.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No supplied version receives a verdict. States marked cannot_determine indicate that the rows cannot establish a supplied version, even where their numerical outcomes are readable. The supplied figure caption and Appendix A disagree about MNIST initialization: the caption says Uniform He, while Appendix A specifies Gaussian He.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or held-out comparison between random and natural labels.
No width sweep past the width needed for zero training error.
No matched comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks on the same image dataset.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.
